extraction.name: FLORES-101 Evaluation Benchmark for Low-Resource and Multilingual Machine Translation
extraction.description: FLORES-101 is an evaluation benchmark consisting of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and professionally translated into 101 languages. The dataset covers a variety of topics and domains including WikiNews, WikiJunior, and WikiVoyage. All translations are multilingually aligned, enabling evaluation of many-to-many multilingual translation systems.
extraction.creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc'Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan
extraction.inLanguage: 101 languages including English, Spanish, French, German, Chinese, Arabic, Hindi, and 95 others
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia sources including Wikinews (international news articles), Wikijunior (age-appropriate nonfiction books for children), and WikiVoyage (travel guide with articles about travel tips, food and destinations). The sentence selection process consisted of selecting an article at random from each source, and then manually selecting a few (typically between 3 and 5) contiguous sentences from each article, avoiding segments with very short or malformed sentences. One paragraph per document was carefully selected from either the beginning, middle or end of the article, with balanced location selection equally distributed across the whole corpus.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: All source sentences were extracted from multiple Wikimedia sources: Wikinews (collection of international news articles), Wikijunior (collection of age-appropriate nonfiction books for children from birth to age 12), and WikiVoyage (travel guide with collection of articles about travel tips, food and destinations around the globe). A third of the sentences came from each source.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The sentence selection process involved selecting an article at random from each source, and then manually selecting a few (typically between 3 and 5) contiguous sentences from each article, avoiding segments with very short or malformed sentences. To avoid bias from document structure, one paragraph per document was carefully selected from either the beginning, middle or end of the article. The location selection was balanced to be equally distributed across the whole corpus. For each sentence, Wikipedia URL, topic, and boolean flags indicating whether the sentence contained entities linked to other Wikipedia pages and images were extracted. All sentences were manually labeled by a more detailed sub-topic, one of 10 possibilities: crime, disasters, entertainment, geography, health, nature, politics, science, sports, and travel.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Translations were performed by professional translators through Language Service Providers (LSPs). The workflow included translation (with editing), followed by quality assurance (QA) performed by an independent LSP. Translation quality was assessed through a Translation Quality Score calculated per language on a 0 to 100 scale, based on the number of identified errors by evaluation LSPs. Errors examined included: grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition or omission of information, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, and register. Each error was associated with a severity level: minor, major, or critical. The acceptable translation quality score was set to 90%. If the score was below the threshold, translations together with the assessment report were sent back to the translation LSP for re-translation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Automatic checks were implemented to ensure translation quality: (i) language identification, (ii) checking whether the translation is a copy of the source sentence, (iii) checking whether the translation has significantly different length, (iv) checking translation fluency according to a language model, (v) checking whether the translation is a copy of the translation produced by publicly available translation engines. A heuristic was proposed to detect and reject professional translations that are likely copies from translation engines based on their sentence-level similarity. Any set of translations with more than 10% of the sentences violating the criteria would need to be re-translated prior to performing any subsequent human evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is divided into three splits: dev, devtest, and test. The dev and devtest sets are publicly downloadable. The test set is not released but is available via a publicly available evaluation server. The test set can be used by various evaluation campaigns, such as the WMT 2021 Large-Scale Multilingual Task. The primary motivation for keeping the test set available only through an evaluation server is to guarantee equivalent assessment of models and reduce overfitting to the test set.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables better assessment of model quality on the long tail of low-resource languages, including the evaluation of many-to-many multilingual translation systems. The majority of the world's population speak low-resource languages and would benefit from improvements in translation quality on their native languages. FLORES-101 supports the measurement of traditionally neglected regionally-relevant pairs such as Xhosa-Zulu, Vietnamese-Thai, and Spanish-Aymara.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: While translationese (or overly literal or awkward translations) has known idiosyncrasies, the authors conjecture that these effects are rather marginal when evaluating models in low-resource languages, where current MT systems produce many severe mistakes. The authors believe the benefits of many-to-many evaluation largely outsize the risk of evaluating translationese. All source sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia, which means source sentences not in English are produced by human translators.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: All source sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia, while considering a broad set of topics that could be of general interest regardless of the native language of the reader. The only caveat is that source sentences not in English are produced by human translators, introducing translationese effects. The dataset focuses on evaluation rather than training, with 3001 sentences per language. Several low-resource languages have relatively few articles containing well structured sentences in Wikipedia. Translating a few hundred sentences for several thousand different language pairs would be infeasible, at the very least because of the lack of qualified professional translators that could read both the source and target side.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluation purposes in machine translation research, specifically for: (i) enabling the evaluation of many-to-many multilingual models, meaning the evaluation of translations from any language to any other language including very long-tail languages; (ii) enabling other kinds of evaluation beyond machine translation, such as document-level translation, multi-modal translation, multilingual classification. The dataset is divided into three splits: dev (for hyper-parameter tuning), devtest (for testing during development phase), and test (for final evaluation through evaluation server). Beyond translation, FLORES-101 can be used to evaluate tasks such as sentence and document classification, language identification, and multilingual domain adaptation.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each sentence was translated once by professional translators, then edited by different translators within the LSP, followed by quality assessment by an independent LSP. If quality was insufficient, re-translation was performed. On average, 1 re-translation was required, with a maximum of 3 re-translations for some languages.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: The sentence selection process was performed by 10 different annotators in the research lab: 6 male and 4 female; with different roles in research (researchers including scientists and engineers, and program/project managers); originally coming from different regions of the world: East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America and North America. Professional translators were used for the actual translation work through Language Service Providers.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automatic checks were implemented including: language identification tools, sentence similarity checks, length difference checks, language model-based fluency checks, and comparison with outputs from publicly available translation engines to detect copying.
